findings.claim: `project.ecMaxContribution` must never be summed across the join to `organization`. evidence.sql: SELECT SUM(ecMaxContribution) FROM project
SELECT SUM(p.ecMaxContribution) FROM project p JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id
SELECT SUM(ecContribution) FROM organization

findings.claim: The per-project EU contribution and the sum of its organisations' EU contributions agree for all but 109 of 35,389 projects, and where they diverge the divergence is large, not rounding - ENG GAM 2018 (id 807085) is committed 171,920,071.33 EUR at project level but its organisation rows sum to 88,470,419.52, and OLGA (id 101036871) has 24,991,644.02 at project level against 0.00 summed across its organisations.

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT p.id, p.ecMaxContribution e, SUM(o.ecContribution) s FROM project p JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id GROUP BY 1,2) t WHERE t.s IS NULL OR ABS(t.e-t.s) > 0.01*t.e

findings.serves: route=sql - grain-choice questions; also a gold-bounds hazard for any hybrid question that reports a single project's EU funding

evidence.key_result: 999997930 CENTRE NATIONAL DE LA RECHERCHE SCIENTIFIQUE CNRS 1871 1885

evidence.sql: SELECT organisationID, COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) np FROM organization WHERE role='coordinator' GROUP BY organisationID ORDER BY np DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT organisationID) FROM organization
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT projectID, organisationID FROM organization GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*)>1)

candidates.why: CNRS has 1,885 rows but only 1,871 distinct projects (411 project-org pairs are duplicated corpus-wide), so even the entity-level count has a within-project double-count.

findings.claim: For country='IT', counting organization rows gives 17,243 while counting distinct projects gives 7,899; the same divergence at coordinator grain for DE is 20,854 rows / 9,955 distinct projects / 3,844 coordinator-role projects. Both numbers of each pair are computed, not asserted.

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM organization WHERE country='IT'
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM organization WHERE country='IT'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM organization WHERE country='DE'
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM organization WHERE country='DE'
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM organization WHERE country='DE' AND role='coordinator'

findings.serves: sql/aggregation; also the reference-answer discipline for any hybrid filter that joins organization

findings.claim: No project has more than one coordinator row, and exactly one project (id 101036871) has none. Near-miss checked: the >1 case is empty, so "exactly one coordinator per project" holds for 35,388 of 35,389.

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT p.id, SUM(CASE WHEN o.role='coordinator' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) c FROM project p JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id GROUP BY p.id) WHERE c>1
SELECT p.id FROM project p JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id GROUP BY p.id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN o.role='coordinator' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)>1
SELECT p.id FROM project p JOIN organization o ON o.projectID=p.id GROUP BY p.id HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN o.role='coordinator' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)=0

findings.serves: sql/lookup, adversarial (a question presuming multiple coordinators is unanswerable)

findings.claim: `organization.role` has exactly 5 values - participant 124,070, coordinator 35,388, thirdParty 11,601, partner 7,658, internationalPartner 215 (178,932 rows total). All 7,658 'partner' rows have NULL ecContribution and are the dominant source of that NULL. The non-participant roles are thin at project grain: thirdParty touches 4,176 projects, partner 2,235, internationalPartner 105.

evidence.sql: SELECT role, COUNT(*) FROM organization GROUP BY role
SELECT role, COUNT(*) FROM organization WHERE ecContribution IS NULL GROUP BY role
SELECT role, COUNT(DISTINCT projectID) FROM organization WHERE role IN ('thirdParty','partner','internationalPartner') GROUP BY role

findings.serves: sql/aggregation and sql/lookup; warns any funding-sum question that filtering by role changes the NULL population

candidates.topic: How many H2020 projects are in each status, and what share were terminated

evidence.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) n FROM project GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT status, fundingScheme, COUNT(*) n FROM project WHERE status='TERMINATED' AND fundingScheme IN ('ERC-STG','SME-1') GROUP BY 1,2

candidates.why: The only three-valued status column, exhaustively enumerable, and a natural "how many were terminated" question with a single verifiable answer.

candidates.topic: Bare `MSCA-IF` versus the whole MSCA-IF* variant family (EF-ST, GF, EF-RI, EF-CAR ...)

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM project WHERE fundingScheme='MSCA-IF'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM project WHERE fundingScheme LIKE 'MSCA-IF%'

candidates.why: "How many Marie Curie Individual Fellowships" has two defensible SQL readings differing by 4,808 projects - a precise trap the drafter must pin down in the question wording.

candidates.topic: Average project duration in months by funding scheme, from startDate/endDate arithmetic
candidates.counts: 14 schemes compared; SME-1 4.14 months to ERC-COG 68.02 months

evidence.sql: SELECT fundingScheme, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(DATEDIFF('month', startDate, endDate)),2) avg_months, MIN(DATEDIFF('month',startDate,endDate)) minm, MAX(DATEDIFF('month',startDate,endDate)) maxm FROM project WHERE fundingScheme IN ('MSCA-IF','RIA','SME-1','MSCA-IF-EF-ST','CSA','ERC-STG','ERC-COG','IA','ERC-ADG','SME-2','ERC-POC','MSCA-ITN','MSCA-RISE','MSCA-COFUND') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY avg_months DESC

candidates.why: Requires real date arithmetic plus a group-by, and the SME-1 vs ERC family spread (4 vs 68 months) makes the answer memorable and checkable.

candidates.topic: Projects whose EC grant signature came AFTER the action had already started (retroactive signature), and the largest lag
candidates.counts: 2,898 projects signed after their start date; max lag 437 days

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ecSignatureDate > startDate) sig_after_start, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ecSignatureDate > endDate) sig_after_end, MAX(DATEDIFF('day',startDate,ecSignatureDate)) maxlag FROM project
SELECT id, acronym, fundingScheme, startDate, endDate, ecSignatureDate FROM project WHERE ecSignatureDate>endDate OR DATEDIFF('day',startDate,ecSignatureDate)=437 ORDER BY id

candidates.why: A three-date comparison the vector route cannot do at all, with a tiny named extreme (2 projects signed after they had already ended) as a natural follow-up.

candidates.topic: The 12 projects with no start or end date - what they all have in common

evidence.sql: SELECT status, fundingScheme, COUNT(*) n FROM project WHERE startDate IS NULL GROUP BY 1,2
SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE startDate IS NULL) null_start, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE endDate IS NULL) null_end, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE endDate < startDate) end_before_start FROM project
SELECT id, acronym FROM project WHERE startDate IS NULL ORDER BY id
evidence.key_result: 653040 CONFAM; 661496 QSIPP; 699995 MULTIZONAL SCAFFOLD; 701561 ASUNDER; 743637 NanoOsmDiode; 753215 APPS; 846299 APApore4RNA; 891212 FLARe; 101024440 GUIDE-AF; 101026554 BREASTCANCERSTEM; 101030725 RADCODE; 101038075 POP1Seed

candidates.why: A fully enumerable 12-row gold set with a clean, surprising invariant - every missing-date project is a terminated individual fellowship.

candidates.topic: The `nature` column - crisis-tagged projects and their timing

evidence.sql: SELECT COALESCE(nature,'(null)') v, COUNT(*) n FROM project GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM project WHERE nature='crisisResponse' AND startDate>=DATE '2020-01-01'
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM project WHERE nature IS NOT NULL AND status='TERMINATED'

candidates.why: A rarely-touched, almost-entirely-null column with an exact-100% temporal fact (all 90 crisisResponse projects started in 2020 or later) that no retrieval route could establish.

findings.claim: "Still running" has two divergent SQL readings: `status='SIGNED'` gives 2,964 projects, while `endDate > DATE '2026-07-29'` gives 1,542 - and 1,441 SIGNED projects have an end date already in the past, while 0 CLOSED projects have a future end date. The status column and the date column disagree on 1,441 projects.

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='SIGNED') signed, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE endDate > DATE '2026-07-29') end_future, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='SIGNED' AND endDate < DATE '2026-07-29') signed_but_ended, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status='CLOSED' AND endDate > DATE '2026-07-29') closed_but_future FROM project

findings.serves: sql filter-count and aggregation; also an adversarial/ambiguous seed - the question "how many projects are still running?" has no single right answer without pinning status vs date.

findings.claim: `legalBasis` on `project` has 40 distinct values, all beginning 'H2020', dominated by H2020-EU.1.3. (11,780 = MSCA) and H2020-EU.1.1. (7,850 = ERC); the long tail runs down to single-project codes, and one row carries three semicolon-joined codes. `frameworkProgramme` is constant 'H2020' and carries no information. masterCall equals subCall in 22,165 of 35,389 projects, so the two are not interchangeable.

evidence.sql: SELECT COALESCE(legalBasis,'(null)') v, COUNT(*) n FROM project GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT masterCall) mc, COUNT(DISTINCT subCall) sc, COUNT(DISTINCT topics) tp, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE masterCall=subCall) mceqsc FROM project

findings.serves: sql filter-count / aggregation; tells drafters that programme-part questions are answerable off `project.legalBasis` alone

findings.claim: Project start dates cluster hard on the 1st of the month and on January and September. January is the largest start month at 5,797 projects (5,488 of them on the 1st), September second at 5,148 (4,766 on the 1st); August is smallest at 1,716. Start-year totals peak in 2019 (5,561) and collapse in 2022 (934) and 2023 (14), with 12 nulls.

evidence.sql: SELECT EXTRACT(month FROM startDate) m, COUNT(*) n, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE EXTRACT(day FROM startDate)=1) day1 FROM project WHERE startDate IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM startDate) y, COUNT(*) n FROM project GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

findings.serves: sql aggregation and date-arithmetic seeds; warns drafters that any "projects starting in year X" question is shaped by the January/September intake and that 2022-2023 are near-empty tails
